why:
MERGED 2026-09-04 during the phase-417 rebase onto main, from two independent rows that both landed -- this branch's W-M2 note and main's own filing. JSON keeps the LAST, so one author's reasoning was being discarded silently. Both said `extension`; the prose is combined here and neither is lost.

Landed 2026-09-04 (`55324cc33`, sched). Ours-only, and there is no upstream name to align to: neither the recorded rclrs nor rclcpp surface contains `jitter` or `late_wake` at all. Returns `(max_release_jitter_us, late_wakes, total_wakes)` from `spin_period` (`executor/spin.rs:2152`). rclcpp has no counterpart because it does not own the wake: an rclcpp executor blocks in `rmw_wait` and a timer that fires late is simply a timer that fired, with nothing recording how late. Here `spin_period` IS the release, so lateness is measurable and is the figure of merit a periodic RTOS task is judged by. The RATIO is why both counters are returned rather than just the max -- one late wake in ten thousand is a glitch, ten thousand in ten thousand means the period cannot be met.

phase-417 W-M2 note: ledgered here because `--require-disposition` armed the api-parity gate and this landed on main in parallel (`55324cc33 feat(sched): measure release jitter`).

RFC-0052's real-time observability: `(max_release_jitter_us, late_wakes, total_wakes)` for a `spin_period` loop. rclcpp has no counterpart because it does not own the release -- a periodic rclcpp node is a wall timer on a general-purpose executor, and the lateness a scheduler introduces is not a quantity rclcpp is in a position to measure. Ours is, because one executor owns one RTOS task (RFC-0002) and the period is the task's own.

The RATIO is the point, not the maximum alone: one late wake in ten thousand is a glitch, ten thousand in ten thousand means the period cannot be met -- two different failures that a single max cannot tell apart. Zero on a clockless build, where `spin_period` refuses to run at all (issue 0709), so there is nothing to have measured.
